texts.facts: 2(d). The defendants have issued notice to the plaintiff and made an attempt to disturb the physical possession and tried to remove the shed stayed in the OS.No. 2431/2024 schedule property. The complaint was lodged to jurisdictional police, but they refused to receive the same. Hence, filed this suit. The defendant school has issued notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed and he requested 3 months time to vacate the same. The children have no place to sit or for class process. In the SDMC and parents meeting dated 18/12/2023, decided to serve the notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest over the schedule premises. The defendant No.1 and 2 have no personal interest and no enmity against the plaintiff, they have been made parties in their individual capacity and prayed for dismissal of the suit. After death of his father, he OS.No. 2431/2024 continued as Watchman on honorary basis without any salary. As such, he filed a suit for permanent injunction against the defendants.
texts.arguments: 10. The counsel for the plaintiff in support of his submissions argued that the plaintiff and his wife are in occupation of suit schedule property. The plaintiff's father since from 1983 was running service OS.No. 2431/2024 in the school as per the advise of the Villagers, as there was illegal activities were going on in the school premises. The plaintiff's father was asked to look after the school premises. Since then the father of plaintiff was stayed in the suit schedule premises and rendering service to the school as honorary as Watchman. The counsel further submits that after the death of father of plaintiff, the plaintiff continued to stay in the suit schedule premises with his wife, who is also working as Aya in the very same school appointed by the Education department. 10(a). The counsel submits that the defendants all of a sudden issued notice demanding the plaintiff to vacate the suit schedule premises and making illegal demand. The plaintiff has no other accommodation to stay. The suit schedule premises/shed has separate ingress and egress. The demolition of shed is not required for construction of 8 new class rooms to the children. The photographs are created by the OS.No. 2431/2024 defendants for the purpose of the case to show that the school has no class rooms and children are sitting outside the school. 10(b). The counsel further submitted that the plaintiff in order to show the possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property since long time, the bank pass book, gas bill address are shown as a suit schedule property. The photograph of Exs.P-8 and P-9 series would show the plaintiff and his wife are staying in the suit schedule premises without any hindrance and they have right to continue in the suit schedule premises. The defendants unnecessarily interfering and prayed to decree the suit. 11. The learned D.G.P. on behalf of the defendants submitted that the plaintiff is not at all connected to defendant school. His wife is working in the school appointed by the Education department as Aya. OS.No. 2431/2024 There is no post called Watchman in the school. The School or Education department have not appointed either father of the plaintiff or plaintiff as a Watchman to render service in the school. It is further submitted that the plaintiff has not placed any material to show that his father was rendering service in the school as Watchman and thereafter plaintiff. The wife of plaintiff was appointed as Aya in the year 1995 and she was transferred to this school subsequently. 11(a). It is further submitted that the Government had sanctioned 8 rooms under "Viveka Shala Yojane" an amount of Rs.1 crore was sanctioned. The dilapidated 3 class rooms have been demolished for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms. The children presently have no class rooms and they are sitting outside the class rooms in the school premises, affecting their educational activities. The counsel submits that thought plaintiff and his wife are OS.No. 2431/2024 staying in the suit schedule premises, their occupation Muniraju M vs Reeni on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40571489/ 6 is unauthorized without any authority either by the School or department. 11(b). The counsel further submits that utmost the plaintiff and his wife staying in the school premises as a licencee on permission, once license or permission are revoked, they have no right or authority to continue. The plaintiff's wife is not party to the suit. She has not filed any suit. The plaintiff is not connected with the suit. The plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands and he is not entitled for discretionary relief of permanent injunction and prayed for dismissal of suit. 12.

First of all there is no material that the Villagers have authorized the plaintiff to render service.

Earlier to that Villagers have no voice in respect of school premises.
The plaintiff has not produced any document to show that from 1981-82 on wards his father was rendering service in the school and stayed in the suit schedule premises.
There is no material on record that the plaintiff and his wife are staying in the suit schedule premises from 1983 on wards.
Admittedly, the plaintiff's wife Jayalakshmamma is working as Aya in the Government Primary School, Saneguruvanahalli.
PW.1 deposed that his wife has transferred to said school and working from 18-12-2003.
The plaintiff has not placed any material that he is staying in the suit schedule premises from 1982-83.
The gas bills and bank pass book are recent documents.

Therefore, the plaintiff and his wife are not staying in the suit schedule premises for long time, on the other hand,
in all probabilities after plaintiff's wife transferred to defendant school appeared to have staying in the suit schedule
Therefore, the possession of plaintiff and his wife in the suit schedule premises is not lawful and it is unauthorize and illegal.
18. The counsel for the plaintiff in the cross- examination of DW.1 has suggested that the plaintiff and his wife are staying in the suit schedule premises from 1996 on permissive possession.

If said OS.No. 2431/2024 suggestion is taken into consideration, assuming that the School or Education department has permitted the plaintiff and his wife to stay in the suit schedule premises, it is only on permission as that of a licensee
Once permission is revoked by issuing notice, the plaintiff and his wife have no business to stay in the suit schedule premises.
19. PW.1 admitted there are 600 children are studying in the school.
Due to shortage of school rooms under "Viveka Shala Yojane" 8 rooms are sanctioned for construction.

9 estimation order are also placed before the Court, which would show Rs.83.40 lakhs was sanctioned for construction of 8 rooms
The existing 3 dilapidated rooms are demolished for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms.
The photographs would depicts presently the children are sitting outside the school building and classes are being conducted due to shortage of school rooms.
The suit schedule premises is situated in the place where the proposed 8 class rooms are to be constructed.
Therefore, the existence of shed for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms is an obstruction.
As per the work order the construction of rooms have to be completed before 28-08-2024.
But, it has not been carried out due to obstruction by the plaintiff and his wife by not vacating the premises.

Therefore, if the construction is not completed within the financial year, there is every chance of lapse of the amount which was granted for construction of class rooms for welfare of the children in the interest of their academic activiti
The issuance of notice by the defendants to the plaintiff's wife to vacate the shed in the school premises cannot be termed as interference.
The plaintiff himself is not in lawful possession of suit schedule premises.

The wife of plaintiff being employee of 'D' group working in the same school, not vacating the premises so as to OS.No. 2431/2024 accommodate construction of 8 rooms for academic activities of the children amounts to misconduct.
20. The plaintiff has not placed any material to hold that he is in lawful possession of suit schedule property.
There is no material since from the time of his father he has been in occupation of suit schedule premises.
The plaintiff has suppressed the material facts.
The suit for permanent injunction, it is a discretionary relief.
The person who approaches the Court must come with clean hands without any suppression.
The plaintiff has not able to establish that he is in lawful possession of suit schedule premises.
His possession is unlawful and unauthorized.
The defendant school has issued notice to vacate the premises.
If the suit is not decreed, the defendants would be put to irreparable loss and injury, there is every chance of lapse of huge amount sanctioned for construction of 8 class rooms.

Therefore, by considering the interest of children OS.No. 2431/2024 studying around 600 students, if the injunction is granted to protect the plaintiff to stay in the schedule premises would affect the educational activities of the children
Permanent injunction cannot be granted against the true owner.
Therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled for injunction.
Accordingly, answered issues No.1 to 4 in the Negative.

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is dismissed with costs.
